flow_cytometry_facs.description: Flow cytometry and fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS) for immunophenotyping, cell sorting, and quantitative analysis of cell surface and intracellular markers using fluorochrome-conjugated antibodies.

gating_hierarchy.description: Sequential gating strategy to identify target cell populations from heterogeneous samples.

standard_immunophenotyping.value_or_range: Time gate -> FSC-A vs SSC-A (exclude debris) -> FSC-H vs FSC-A (singlets) -> Viability dye negative (live cells) -> Lineage markers
standard_immunophenotyping.when: Standard multi-color immunophenotyping of PBMCs or tissue-derived cells
standard_immunophenotyping.why: Sequential cleaning removes debris, doublets, and dead cells before phenotyping to prevent false positives. Dead cells have high autofluorescence and nonspecific antibody binding.

rare_population_detection.value_or_range: Add dump channel (Lin-) gate before target population gating; collect >500,000 total events
rare_population_detection.when: Target population is <1% of parent (e.g., antigen-specific T cells, circulating tumor cells)
rare_population_detection.why: Rare populations require stringent exclusion of false positives and high event counts for statistical power. Need at least 100 events in target gate for reliable quantification.

common_mistakes: Skipping singlet discrimination, leading to doublet artifacts that mimic double-positive populations
Not using viability dye, causing dead cell autofluorescence to appear as false positives
Setting gates on unstained controls instead of FMO controls in multicolor panels
Gating too tightly on FSC/SSC, excluding activated or blasting lymphocytes which are larger

compensation.description: Mathematical correction for spectral overlap between fluorochromes detected in multiple channels.

panels_up_to_4_colors.value_or_range: Standard compensation using single-stained controls (beads or cells)
panels_up_to_4_colors.when: Simple 4-color panels with well-separated fluorochromes (e.g., FITC, PE, PerCP, APC)
panels_up_to_4_colors.why: Minimal spectral overlap between these classic fluorochromes; standard compensation is usually sufficient.

panels_5_to_12_colors.value_or_range: Compensation matrix required; use single-stained compensation beads; spread fluorochromes across multiple lasers
panels_5_to_12_colors.when: Multi-color panels where spectral overlap becomes significant
panels_5_to_12_colors.why: Compensation errors compound with more fluorochromes. Spreading across lasers (405nm, 488nm, 561nm, 640nm) minimizes spillover between channels on same laser.

panels_above_12_colors.value_or_range: Consider spectral flow cytometry; if conventional, use automated compensation with rigorous single-stained controls and FMO for every marker
panels_above_12_colors.when: High-dimensional panels (>12 colors) or full spectral cytometry (30+ markers)
panels_above_12_colors.why: Conventional compensation becomes unreliable above 12-15 colors due to compounding spillover. Spectral cytometry uses full emission spectra and unmixing algorithms instead.

common_mistakes: Using cells for compensation when beads would provide brighter, more consistent single-stained controls
Not matching compensation control fluorochrome brightness to experimental antibodies
Ignoring autofluorescence subtraction, especially for myeloid cells and macrophages
Under-compensating PE-Cy7 spillover into PE channel, a notoriously problematic pair

fluorochrome_panel_design.description: Matching fluorochrome brightness to antigen expression density for optimal signal-to-noise.

low_density_antigens.value_or_range: Use brightest fluorochromes: PE, APC, PE-Cy7, BV421
low_density_antigens.when: Detecting low-abundance markers (CCR7, CXCR5, IL-4, IL-17, cytokines, chemokine receptors)
low_density_antigens.why: Low-density antigens produce weak signals; bright fluorochromes maximize signal-to-noise ratio and resolution between positive and negative populations.

high_density_antigens.value_or_range: Can use dimmer fluorochromes: FITC, PerCP-Cy5.5, APC-Cy7, BV510
high_density_antigens.when: Detecting highly expressed markers (CD3, CD4, CD8, CD45, CD19, CD20)
high_density_antigens.why: High-abundance antigens generate strong signals even with dim fluorochromes, freeing bright channels for harder-to-detect markers.

common_mistakes: Putting a dim marker (e.g., cytokine) on a dim fluorochrome, making it undetectable
Not considering tandem dye degradation (PE-Cy7 and APC-Cy7 are light-sensitive)
Placing two markers with high spillover on co-expressed markers, creating resolution artifacts
Not titrating antibodies - more is not better; excess antibody increases background

minimum_events.description: Number of events to collect for statistically reliable quantification.

standard_immunophenotyping.when: Analyzing major populations (T cells, B cells) that are >5% of parent gate
standard_immunophenotyping.why: Provides CV <5% for populations >5% of parent. Standard for clinical and research immunophenotyping.

rare_populations.value_or_range: 500,000-1,000,000 total events; aim for >100 events in target population
rare_populations.when: Target population <0.1% (e.g., antigen-specific T cells, regulatory T cells in some contexts, CTCs)
rare_populations.why: Poisson statistics: need N>100 in target gate for CV <10%. For 0.01% population, need 1,000,000 total events to get 100 target events.

common_mistakes: Collecting 10,000 total events and trying to quantify a 0.1% population (only 10 events - unreliable)
Not accounting for gating losses when calculating required acquisition events
Comparing percentages of rare populations without considering absolute event counts

fmo_controls.description: Fluorescence Minus One controls - sample stained with all fluorochromes except one to reveal spillover-driven spread.

essential_use.value_or_range: Run FMO for every marker in panels >4 colors
essential_use.when: Setting gates for markers with continuous expression (activation markers, chemokine receptors) or when positive/negative boundary is unclear
essential_use.why: FMOs reveal the true spread of fluorescence from other channels into the channel of interest. Without FMOs, gates based on unstained controls will be set too low, creating false positives.

can_be_reduced.value_or_range: Run FMOs only for difficult-to-gate markers after panel validation
can_be_reduced.when: Well-validated panel with clearly bimodal populations (e.g., CD4 vs CD8)
can_be_reduced.why: Once panel is validated and gates are established, bimodal markers (clear positive/negative) may not need FMOs every run. But continuous markers always need FMOs.

common_mistakes: Using isotype controls instead of FMOs for gate setting in multicolor panels
Not running FMOs for markers on a continuum (e.g., PD-1, CD25, CCR7)
Assuming FMOs from one experiment apply to another with different instrument settings

common_cell_type_markers.description: Standard surface markers for identifying major immune cell populations.

t_cell_subsets.value_or_range: CD3+CD4+ (helper), CD3+CD8+ (cytotoxic); Naive: CD45RA+CCR7+; Central memory: CD45RA-CCR7+; Effector memory: CD45RA-CCR7-; TEMRA: CD45RA+CCR7-
t_cell_subsets.when: Immunophenotyping T cell differentiation states in peripheral blood
t_cell_subsets.why: CD45RA and CCR7 define the four canonical memory subsets. CD62L can substitute for CCR7 but CCR7 is preferred for human samples.

b_cells.value_or_range: CD19+ or CD20+; Memory: CD27+; Naive: CD27-IgD+; Switched memory: CD27+IgD-; Plasmablasts: CD27hiCD38hi
b_cells.when: B cell subset analysis in blood or lymphoid tissue
b_cells.why: CD19 is the pan-B cell marker; CD27 distinguishes memory from naive. CD20 is lost on plasmablasts/plasma cells.

nk_cells.value_or_range: CD3-CD56+; CD56bright CD16- (cytokine producing); CD56dim CD16+ (cytotoxic)
nk_cells.when: NK cell identification and functional subset analysis
nk_cells.why: CD3 negativity excludes NKT cells. CD56/CD16 distinguish two major functional NK subsets.

monocyte_subsets.value_or_range: Classical: CD14++CD16-; Intermediate: CD14++CD16+; Non-classical: CD14+CD16++
monocyte_subsets.why: Three monocyte subsets have distinct functional properties; intermediate monocytes are expanded in inflammatory conditions.

dendritic_cells.value_or_range: Lin-HLA-DR+; cDC1: CD141(BDCA3)+; cDC2: CD1c(BDCA1)+; pDC: CD303(BDCA2)+CD123+
dendritic_cells.when: DC subset identification in blood or tissue
dendritic_cells.why: DCs are rare (0.1-1% of PBMCs) and require lineage exclusion. BDCA markers distinguish the three major DC subsets with distinct functions.

common_mistakes: Forgetting to exclude CD3+ cells when identifying NK cells, leading to NKT contamination
Using CD20 alone for B cells and missing plasmablasts (CD20-)
Not using lineage dump channel for DC identification, leading to contamination by monocytes

flow_cytometry_facs.best_practice_notes: Always titrate antibodies to optimal concentration (not manufacturer recommended). Include single-stained compensation controls, FMO controls for continuous markers, and unstained controls. For multicolor panels, spread fluorochromes across multiple lasers and match fluorochrome brightness to antigen density. Viability dye is mandatory. Acquire sufficient events for the rarest population of interest.

cell_cycle_analysis.description: Quantitative analysis of cell cycle phase distribution (G0/G1, S, G2/M) using DNA content staining and flow cytometry, with optional thymidine analog incorporation (EdU/BrdU) for S-phase kinetics.

dna_stain_selection.description: Choice of DNA-binding fluorescent dye determines fixation requirements, laser compatibility, and multiparameter capability.

standard_fixed_cell_analysis.value_or_range: Propidium iodide (PI) at 50 ug/mL with RNase A (100 ug/mL)
standard_fixed_cell_analysis.when: Standard cell cycle analysis on fixed cells using 488nm laser
standard_fixed_cell_analysis.why: PI intercalates into double-stranded nucleic acids. RNase treatment is essential to eliminate RNA staining which distorts DNA histograms. Compatible with most standard flow cytometers.

live_cell_analysis.value_or_range: Hoechst 33342 at 5-10 ug/mL for 30-60 min at 37C
live_cell_analysis.when: Live cell sorting by cell cycle phase, or combining with surface markers on live cells
live_cell_analysis.why: Hoechst 33342 is cell-permeant and does not require fixation. Requires UV laser (355nm). Slight AT-base preference but acceptable for cell cycle.

multiparameter_with_antibodies.when: Combining DNA content with intracellular antibody staining (e.g., cyclin expression, phospho-histone H3)
multiparameter_with_antibodies.why: DAPI requires UV laser (355nm) but does not interfere with FITC/PE/APC channels, enabling multiparameter analysis. Not compatible with PI which overlaps with PE.

common_mistakes: Omitting RNase when using PI, causing inflated S-phase and broad G1 peaks due to RNA staining
Using PI on live cells without fixation - PI only enters dead cells, so it becomes a viability dye not a cell cycle dye
Not allowing sufficient staining time - minimum 30 min for PI, ideally overnight at 4C for best CV
Using Hoechst 33342 at too high concentration causing toxicity and cell cycle arrest

sub_g1_analysis.description: Detection of hypodiploid (sub-G1) DNA content as an indicator of apoptosis.

apoptosis_indicator.value_or_range: Sub-G1 peak with DNA content <2N; gate broadly to include all sub-G1 events
apoptosis_indicator.when: Cells treated with apoptosis-inducing agents, drug screening
apoptosis_indicator.why: Apoptotic DNA fragmentation produces nuclei with reduced DNA content appearing left of the G1 peak. However, sub-G1 is not 100% specific for apoptosis.

debris_discrimination.value_or_range: Use pulse processing (FSC-H vs FSC-A) and set lower FSC threshold to exclude debris while retaining apoptotic nuclei
debris_discrimination.when: Distinguishing true apoptotic sub-G1 events from cellular debris
debris_discrimination.why: Debris has very low FSC and random fluorescence. Apoptotic nuclei retain some FSC signal. Confirm with Annexin V/PI or caspase assay.

common_mistakes: Interpreting all sub-G1 events as apoptosis without confirmatory assay - mechanical damage also produces sub-G1
Gating too tightly on intact cells and excluding apoptotic nuclei from analysis
Not accounting for cell type-specific differences in apoptotic DNA fragmentation kinetics

minimum_cell_count.description: Number of events required for reliable cell cycle phase distribution estimates.

standard_analysis.value_or_range: 10,000-20,000 singlet events in the analysis gate
standard_analysis.when: Standard cell cycle distribution analysis with all phases represented
standard_analysis.why: At p<0.05, need N>400 in the smallest phase. S-phase is typically 15-30% of cells, so 10,000 total events gives 1,500-3,000 S-phase events. 20,000 events recommended for CV <5%.

sub_g1_or_polyploid_detection.value_or_range: 50,000+ events if sub-G1 or >4N populations are rare (<5%)
sub_g1_or_polyploid_detection.when: Detecting minor apoptotic fractions or polyploid populations
sub_g1_or_polyploid_detection.why: Rare events (<5%) require more total events for statistical reliability. Need at least 100-400 events in the sub-G1 or polyploid gate.

common_mistakes: Collecting too few events for meaningful phase distribution, especially after gating losses
Not excluding doublets, which create a false 4N peak mimicking G2/M

mathematical_models.description: Algorithms for deconvolving overlapping cell cycle phases from DNA histograms.

dean_jett_fox.value_or_range: Dean-Jett-Fox model in FlowJo or similar software
dean_jett_fox.when: General-purpose cell cycle modeling; good for samples with clear G1 and G2 peaks and moderate S-phase
dean_jett_fox.why: Uses polynomial for S-phase estimation and Gaussian fits for G1/G2. More flexible than Watson for asymmetric or broad S-phase distributions.

watson_pragmatic.when: Clean data with well-defined G1 and G2/M peaks and low debris
watson_pragmatic.why: Watson model assumes simpler S-phase distribution. Works well for high-quality data but may give discrepant results with Dean-Jett-Fox on the same data. Report which model was used.

common_mistakes: Not reporting which mathematical model was used, making results non-reproducible
Applying models to poor-quality histograms with high CV (>8%) on G1 peak
Not constraining G2/G1 ratio to ~2.0 when appropriate, leading to incorrect fits

edu_pulse_duration.description: Duration of EdU or BrdU pulse labeling to mark S-phase cells.

short_pulse_snapshot.when: Measuring S-phase fraction at a single timepoint; cells with doubling time 18-24h
short_pulse_snapshot.why: Short pulse labels only cells actively in S-phase at time of labeling. EdU is detectable in as little as 3 minutes but 15-30 min gives robust signal.

cumulative_labeling.when: Maximizing detection of S-phase cells across a broader window, or cells with slow proliferation
cumulative_labeling.why: Longer pulse captures more cells transiting through S-phase, increasing sensitivity but losing temporal precision.

s_phase_duration_measurement.value_or_range: Dual EdU/BrdU pulse-chase with 1.5-5.5h chase intervals
s_phase_duration_measurement.when: Measuring actual S-phase duration in asynchronous cultures
s_phase_duration_measurement.why: Sequential pulses with different analogs and timed chases allow calculation of S-phase transit time via linear regression of double-positive fraction over time.

common_mistakes: Using EdU concentration too high (>20 uM) causing toxicity and S-phase arrest
Not accounting for EdU-induced DNA damage in long-term experiments
Comparing pulse-labeled fractions between cell lines with different doubling times without normalization

cell_cycle_analysis.best_practice_notes: Always include RNase with PI staining. Report the mathematical model used. Collect 10,000-20,000 gated singlet events minimum. For EdU experiments, include unlabeled control to set EdU-positive gate. Doublet discrimination is critical because doublets of two G1 cells mimic G2/M cells. CV on G1 peak should be <8% for reliable modeling, ideally <5%.

cell_senescence_and_apoptosis.description: Assays for detecting cellular senescence (irreversible growth arrest) and apoptosis (programmed cell death), including SA-beta-gal, Annexin V/PI, and molecular markers.

sa_beta_gal_ph.description: Senescence-associated beta-galactosidase activity detected at specific pH values.

senescence_specific_ph6.why: Normal lysosomal beta-gal is active at pH 4.0. Senescent cells accumulate enlarged lysosomes with increased beta-gal that remains active at the suboptimal pH 6.0. Activity at pH 6.0 is the senescence-specific readout.

non_senescent_lysosomal_ph4.why: All cells have lysosomal beta-gal active at pH 4.0. This is NOT a senescence marker. Used as positive control for enzyme activity.

common_mistakes: Using pH 4.0 and claiming senescence detection
Relying on SA-beta-gal alone without confirming with additional markers (p21, p16)
Not controlling staining time rigorously - overstaining produces false positives
SA-beta-gal is not 100% specific: apoptotic cells and macrophages can also stain positive

annexin_v_pi_quadrants.description: Annexin V binds phosphatidylserine (PS) exposed on apoptotic cells; PI enters cells with compromised membranes.

early_apoptosis.why: Early apoptotic cells flip PS to outer leaflet but exclude PI. Transient state lasting minutes to hours.

late_apoptosis_secondary_necrosis.when: Both PS exposed and membrane compromised
late_apoptosis_secondary_necrosis.why: Cannot distinguish late apoptosis from secondary necrosis by Annexin V/PI alone.

necrosis.when: Primary necrosis - membrane rupture without PS externalization
necrosis.why: Typically small quadrant; large populations suggest mechanical damage.

common_mistakes: Not using calcium-containing binding buffer (1-3 mM Ca2+)
Prolonged PI incubation causing false positives in viable cells
Fixing cells before Annexin V staining
Interpreting Annexin V+/PI+ as exclusively late apoptosis
Using excessive PI concentration (>1 ug/mL) causing cytotoxicity

senescence_markers_by_context.description: Multiple molecular markers should be used in combination.

oncogene_induced_senescence.when: Detecting OIS in tumor suppression studies
oncogene_induced_senescence.why: OIS engages p16/Rb pathway. p16 most reliable for OIS. gamma-H2AX marks persistent DDR.

replicative_senescence.value_or_range: p21 (early), p16INK4a (late), telomere dysfunction foci (TIFs), SA-beta-gal
replicative_senescence.when: Detecting replicative senescence from telomere shortening
replicative_senescence.why: p21 induced first via p53. p16 accumulates later. TIFs confirm telomere-driven senescence.

therapy_induced_senescence.value_or_range: gamma-H2AX foci, p21, SA-beta-gal, SASP factors (IL-6, IL-8)
therapy_induced_senescence.why: Persistent DDR signaling. gamma-H2AX foci persist months after IR. SASP confirms functional phenotype.

common_mistakes: Using single marker to define senescence

sasp_measurement.description: Quantification of senescence-associated secretory phenotype factors.

core_sasp_panel.value_or_range: IL-6, IL-8 (CXCL8), MCP-1 (CCL2), MMP-3, PAI-1, IL-1beta, TNF-alpha
core_sasp_panel.why: IL-6 and IL-8 most conserved SASP factors. Measure by ELISA or multiplex.

conditioned_media_collection.value_or_range: Serum-free or 0.5% serum for 24-48h; IL-6 typically 50-100 pg/mL senescent fibroblasts
conditioned_media_collection.why: Serum interferes with detection. ELISA threshold ~10 pg/mL.

common_mistakes: Not accounting for cell type differences in SASP composition

cell_senescence_and_apoptosis.best_practice_notes: Define senescence by multiple criteria: growth arrest (Ki67-), SA-beta-gal at pH 6.0, molecular markers (p16/p21), SASP. No single marker sufficient. For apoptosis, combine Annexin V/PI with caspase-3 or TUNEL.

cfse_cell_proliferation.description: Tracking cell division by dilution of fluorescent dyes (CFSE, CellTrace Violet) that halve with each division.

cfse_standard.value_or_range: 1-5 uM CFSE for 10-15 min at 37C in serum-free PBS
cfse_standard.why: 1 uM minimum for resolving generations; 5 uM brighter but may be toxic. Titrate per cell type.

celltrace_violet.value_or_range: 2.5-5 uM CellTrace Violet for 20 min at 37C in dark
celltrace_violet.when: Multicolor experiments needing FITC channel; GFP-expressing cells
celltrace_violet.why: CTV on 405nm laser, freeing 488nm channels. 5 uM resolves 5-6 peaks. >2.5 uM may retard sensitive cells.

sensitive_cell_types.when: Primary cells, stem cells, sensitive to toxicity
sensitive_cell_types.why: Fewer resolvable generations (4-5) but maintains viability.

maximum_generations.why: After 8 divisions, signal is 1/256 of original.

practical_limit.why: Peak broadening reduces resolution beyond gen 5-6.

common_mistakes: Not gating on viable cells first

division_index.value_or_range: Average divisions for ALL cells (including undivided). Range: 0+. Formula: sum(i*N(i)/2^i)/sum(N(i)/2^i)
division_index.why: Includes undivided cells. Reflects responder fraction.

proliferation_index.value_or_range: Average divisions for RESPONDING cells only. Range: >=1
proliferation_index.why: Separates responder frequency from division extent.

percent_divided.value_or_range: Fraction that divided at least once. 0-100%
percent_divided.why: Simple metric. Combine with proliferation index.

common_mistakes: Confusing division index with proliferation index - different definitions in FlowJo vs ModFit

cfse_cell_proliferation.best_practice_notes: Include unstimulated control. Titrate dye. Report percent divided AND division/proliferation index. CTV when FITC needed. Label at 1e6/mL serum-free.

cancer_copy_number_analysis.description: Detection and characterization of somatic copy number alterations in cancer genomes.

minimum_tumor_purity.description: Minimum tumor cell fraction for reliable CNA detection.

standard_cna_detection.value_or_range: >30% for broad CNA; >50% for subclonal events
standard_cna_detection.why: At 30% purity, single-copy gain log2R ~0.18. Below 20%, tools fail.

platform_resolution.description: WGS vs WES vs SNP array resolution.
common_mistakes: WES for gene-poor region focal events

logr_ratio_thresholds.description: Log2 ratio thresholds for CNA calling.

standard.why: Pure diploid: loss=log2(1/2)=-1.0; gain=log2(3/2)=0.585. Must purity-adjust.

focal.why: Focal amps (ERBB2, MYC) and dels (CDKN2A, PTEN) harbor drivers.

common_mistakes: Not separating focal from arm-level in GISTIC2

disambiguation.value_or_range: Use ABSOLUTE (outperforms ASCAT); compare with pathology purity
disambiguation.why: Tetraploid with even CN indistinguishable from diploid at half purity.

wgd_detection.value_or_range: WGD if >50% autosomal genome has ASCN >=2 both alleles
wgd_detection.why: 30-40% of tumors have WGD. Affects all downstream analysis.

cancer_copy_number_analysis.best_practice_notes: Report purity and ploidy. Use allele-specific methods. GISTIC2 for recurrent focal events. Compare algorithmic purity with pathology.

nmf_cancer_subtypes.description: NMF for unsupervised cancer subtype discovery using consensus clustering.

cophenetic_correlation.value_or_range: Screen k=2 to k=10+; select at cophenetic drop-off
cophenetic_correlation.why: First major drop = data no longer supports that many clusters.

common_mistakes: Selecting k at cophenetic maximum not drop-off
k=2 always most stable - not necessarily best

random.why: Diversity across runs is basis of consensus.

nndsvd.why: Data-driven, converges faster. Use NNDSVDa for zeros.

nmf_cancer_subtypes.best_practice_notes: Screen k=2-10+ with 50-200 runs. Cophenetic drop-off + silhouette + consensus visualization. Validate with independent data. Pre-filter top 5000 variable genes. Log-transform and mean-center.

somatic_mutation_detection.description: Somatic SNV and indel detection in cancer genomes using Mutect2 and related tools.

wgs.why: At 60x/50% purity, ~15 supporting reads for het variant.

wes.why: Variable coverage; higher depth compensates. 200x detects VAF ~5%.

subclonal.why: Need deeper sequencing; distinguish from artifacts.

minimum_filter.why: Below 5% at standard depth, errors dominate.

common_mistakes: Low VAF misinterpreted as subclonal vs low purity
Not considering CN state on VAF

paired.value_or_range: Always use when available; blood preferred

mutect2.value_or_range: FilterMutectCalls defaults: TLOD>=5.3, contamination, orientation bias

somatic_mutation_detection.best_practice_notes: Matched normal when possible. PoN of 20-50 for tumor-only. FilterMutectCalls defaults. Report purity. Ensemble calling for clinical. Validate key findings.

cosinor_circadian_analysis.description: Statistical analysis of circadian rhythms estimating mesor, amplitude, acrophase.

minimum.why: Practically need 2-4h for reliable estimation. Two cycles minimum.

optimal.why: 30-min reliable for all parameters. >120 min fails period detection.

fixed.why: Period locked by zeitgebers. Improves parameter estimation power.

mesor.why: Differs from arithmetic mean with unequal sampling.

amplitude.why: Reduced = dampened rhythm. Report with CI.

common_mistakes: Amplitude as full range not half

jtk_cycle.value_or_range: Non-parametric; symmetric waveforms; robust to outliers

cosinor.why: CIs enable statistical comparison. Non-equidistant OK.

cosinor_circadian_analysis.best_practice_notes: Sample every 2-4h, >=48h. Fix 24h under entrainment. Report mesor/amplitude/acrophase with CIs. CircaCompare for group comparison. Multiple testing correction.

bone_micro_ct_morphometry.description: Quantitative bone microarchitecture analysis using micro-CT per ASBMR nomenclature.

trabecular.why: BV/TV primary mass measure. Report all four minimum.

distal_femur.value_or_range: 0.1-0.5 mm proximal to growth plate; extend 1-2 mm; exclude cortex

proximal_tibia.value_or_range: 0.1-0.3 mm distal to growth plate; extend 1-1.5 mm

mid_diaphysis.value_or_range: 50 slices above/below midpoint (~1 mm at 10 um)

common_mistakes: Not excluding cortical shell from trabecular ROI

global.value_or_range: Fixed from histogram; Otsu; report value

bone_micro_ct_morphometry.best_practice_notes: Follow Bouxsein 2010 guidelines. Report scan medium, voltage, voxel, ROI, threshold. ASBMR nomenclature. 3D direct measurements preferred.

multiplexed_tissue_imaging.description: Highly multiplexed imaging (CyCIF, CODEX, IMC, MIBI) with segmentation, phenotyping, spatial analysis.

stardist.why: Excels at touching nuclei separation. Fast.

core_tme.value_or_range: DAPI, panCK, Vimentin, aSMA, CD31, CD45, CD3, CD8, CD4, FOXP3, CD20, CD68, CD11c, Ki67, PD-L1, PD-1, GzmB
core_tme.why: Captures tumor, stroma, vasculature, immune subsets, functional states.

multiplexed_tissue_imaging.best_practice_notes: Deep learning segmentation. DAPI + membrane marker. Positive/negative markers per type. Pathologist validation.

western_blot_quantification.description: Densitometric protein quantification from Western blots.

total_protein.value_or_range: Ponceau S, stain-free, SYPRO Ruby, Coomassie
total_protein.why: Less susceptible to expression changes. Linear 10-50 ug.

housekeeping_acceptable.when: Verified stable; loading 1-10 ug in linear range

housekeeping_fails.why: These proteins change under experimental conditions.

determine.when: Before quantitative experiment; each new antibody
determine.why: Both target and control must be linear.

exposure.why: ECL non-linear at high intensity. Fluorescent wider range.

minimum.why: Minimum for statistics. Technical replicates insufficient.

western_blot_quantification.best_practice_notes: Total protein normalization preferred. Linear range titration. Fluorescent for wider range. n>=3 biological replicates. Never quantify saturated bands.

hemodynamic_analysis.description: Cardiovascular hemodynamic parameters: blood pressure, cardiac output, vascular resistance, HRV.

standard.value_or_range: MAP = (SBP + 2*DBP)/3. Normal: 70-105 mmHg. Min perfusion: 60 mmHg

direct.why: True MAP. 1/3 formula overestimates at high HR.

frequency_domain.why: HF=respiratory sinus arrhythmia. LF interpretation debated.

cfpwv.value_or_range: cfPWV gold standard. Normal <10 m/s; risk >10 m/s

hemodynamic_analysis.best_practice_notes: Report MAP method. Standardize HRV recording duration. Both time and frequency domain. Remove ectopics. cfPWV gold standard. ESC/NASPE guidelines.

amyloid_plaque_quantification.description: Quantitative amyloid-beta plaque burden assessment in brain tissue for AD research.

congo_red.when: Fibrillar amyloid confirmation; CAA vs parenchymal

ihc.when: ALL plaques including diffuse; total burden
ihc.why: Both fibrillar and diffuse. 6E10 cross-reacts APP.

area_fraction.why: Most commonly reported. Correlates biochemical Abeta.

regions.why: Distribution varies by region and model. Report separately.

stereology_sections.why: Guard zones needed. SRS through full ROI extent.

amyloid_plaque_quantification.best_practice_notes: ThioS/Congo Red for fibrillar; IHC for all. Stereology with SRS gold standard. Min 8 sections. Cortex/hippocampus separately. Validate automated thresholds.

glycosylation_prediction.description: Computational prediction of N- and O-linked glycosylation sites with sequon rules and species considerations.

proline.value_or_range: Pro at +1 abolishes; Pro at +3 and -1 inhibit
proline.why: Prevents required tight turn for OST binding.

structure.value_or_range: Must be in accessible loop/turn; 78% glycosylated Asn in loops
structure.why: OST acts co-translationally in ER. Buried sequons not glycosylated.

accuracy.why: No consensus. 20 GalNAc-T isoforms. Competition with phosphorylation.

mammalian.value_or_range: CHO: no alpha-2,6-sialylTF; HEK293 more human-like; mouse: Neu5Gc

non_mammalian.value_or_range: Insect: paucimannose; Yeast: high-mannose immunogenic; Plant: xylose + alpha-1,3-fucose immunogenic

glycosylation_prediction.best_practice_notes: N-glyc: scan N-X-S/T; use NetNGlyc or structure tools; validate MS. O-glyc: ~70% accuracy; ISOGlyP for isoform-specific. Always validate experimentally. Account for expression system.
